9.x: IAM policies cannot restrict root (SCPs can, but only in member accounts). Enable MFA, never use root day-to-day, and use break-glass admin roles.

10.q: You need explicit deny rules at the subnet boundary. Which control?
10.x: NACLs are the subnet-level, stateless filter with numbered allow and deny rules; security groups are stateful and allow-only, so they cannot deny.

3.q: A company needs automatic, scheduled rotation of its encryption keys. Which KMS feature?
3.x: Enable it on the customer managed key; the period is configurable (90–2,560 days, default one year) and rotation is transparent to applications.

16.x: Since January 2023, S3 applies SSE-S3 to all new objects by default; setting the bucket default lets you choose SSE-KMS instead. It applies to new uploads, not existing objects.

17.q: An application needs FIPS-validated cryptography. Which KMS consideration?
17.x: KMS HSMs are FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated, and KMS offers FIPS endpoints; check the region's compliance scope.

14.x: S3 Select filters one object server-side; Athena queries many objects with SQL. Note that AWS closed S3 Select to new customers in July 2024 and recommends Athena or S3 Object Lambda instead.

12.a: Exceeding free limits or credits, or leaving resources running after the free period ends
12.x: Since July 2025, new accounts get credits on a free plan of up to six months; older accounts keep the 12-month Free Tier. Set budgets and billing alerts from day one.
